workflowIdentity.workflowTitle: Klinswork Project Change and Documentation Workflow
workflowIdentity.workflowPurpose: Define the complete controlled cycle for selecting a project milestone, preserving the pre-work understanding in a structured intention record, planning and performing the work in a bounded session, testing the intended result, documenting what actually occurred, reconciling project and integration state, evaluating the planning template, generating publication artifacts, updating indexes, and closing the run.

revisionSummary: Moved the workflow start from the work session to a pre-work project review.
Added a preserved work-session intention record with explicit definition of done, anticipated integrations, and planned acceptance tests.
Separated the durable project roadmap from the session-specific implementation plan.
Defined a fresh ChatGPT conversation as a bounded execution environment with a registered context package.
Added plan amendments that preserve rather than rewrite the original intention baseline.
Added planned tests, real-use verification, and evidence collection before the documentation checkpoint.
Moved project and integration reconciliation into the post-work analysis and debrief cycle.
Added evaluation of the work-session-intention template for effectiveness and efficiency after project records are updated.
Added integration IDs, lifecycle references, authority rules, and integration coverage declarations.
Changed the sidecar target from the v2 draft to a future project-aware v3 draft.
Retained publication, catalog, image, Google Sites, communication, and final verification stages.
Added a stopping rule so routine documentation production does not recursively trigger another full documentation run.
workflowRevision.predecessorRelationship: Revises klinswork-documentation-workflow from schema 1.0-draft by moving the cycle earlier, adding intention and debrief controls, strengthening project and integration authority, and retaining publication stages.
compatibilityNotes: Publication, catalog, image, Google Sites, communication, and final-verification stages remain part of the workflow.
The sidecar target moves from the v2 draft toward a project-aware v3 structure.
The new workflow preserves prior planning and intention state instead of rewriting it after execution.
migrationNotes: Runs created under the earlier workflow may not contain intention baselines, amendments, integration coverage, or intention-template evaluations.
Legacy records should be labeled rather than silently upgraded or treated as complete under the revised workflow.

changeHistory.description: The workflow was revised into the current 30-step project-change documentation and publication cycle.

general.summary: The Klinswork Project Change and Documentation Workflow is a reusable 30-step specification that begins with project context and an approved intention, continues through bounded execution and evidence collection, and ends with reconciliation, publication, indexing, communication, and closure.
keyPoints: Roadmaps and implementation plans are separate artifacts.
A fresh work conversation receives bounded context.
Tests and evidence precede the documentation checkpoint.
Project and integration authorities are reconciled before publication.
The planning template is evaluated after reconciliation.
Individual sidecars remain available after catalog aggregation.
Canonical URLs and portal references are verified.
Routine documentation does not recursively trigger another full run.

technical.summary: The source is a JSON workflow specification containing one workflow identity block, 20 states, 11 global input types, 22 global output types, 13 instruction sets, 11 phases, 30 ordered steps, blocking and non-blocking validation conditions, 8 resolved design decisions, and 10 open or planned design decisions.
keyPoints: The specification is declarative JSON; it does not execute the workflow.

projectSpecificLessons: The documentation cycle must begin before implementation so the original understanding can be preserved.
Project, integration, intention, plan, summary, debrief, sidecar, catalog, and run records require separate authority.
A work-session conversation is part of the workflow record and should receive bounded context.
